title: 3D-4CH reaches the halfway point: building Europe’s 3D digital heritage community
content:
18 months into the project, 3D-4CH has reached an important milestone. The Online Competence Centre in 3D for Cultural Heritage is live, a growing community is coming together around 3D cultural heritage, and new opportunities for learning, collaboration and innovation are taking shape across Europe. With another 18 months ahead, the project is now ready to build on this momentum and turn its foundations into lasting impact.

The first half of 3D-4CH has been about turning a shared vision into something tangible: a European online hub where cultural heritage professionals can learn, discover tools, share knowledge and explore new ways of working with 3D.

Since the launch of the 3D-4CH Online Competence Centre in 3D for Cultural Heritage on 28 January 2026, the platform has continued to grow. At Month 18, it already brings together 7 online courses across 6 thematic modules, 45 tools and 80 Knowledge Base resources, alongside storytelling scenarios, events and news. With multilingual content and automatically generated subtitles for Knowledge Base videos, the Centre is designed to make 3D knowledge more accessible to professionals across Europe.

title: International Conference: Preserving and Promoting Europe’s Sporting Heritage
content:
The My Sporting Heritage project consortium, together with Sport & Citoyenneté and Radiona.org – Zagreb Makerspace, invites you to join the international conference My Sporting Heritage: Preserving and Promoting Europe’s Sporting Heritage, taking place on 12 September 2026 at the Technical Museum Nikola Tesla in Zagreb and online.

The conference is intended for researchers, educators, sport organisations and professionals, museum and cultural heritage professionals, curators, historians, students, digital practitioners, game-based learning professionals and everyone interested in sport and its cultural heritage.

My Sporting Heritage is an Erasmus+ Sport project exploring how Europe’s sporting heritage can be preserved, interpreted, shared and made accessible to different communities and generations. The project brings together expertise from museums, academia, cultural heritage, sport, digital culture and participatory practices.
